clue.text: Irishman joins church for spiritual event

blocks.note: Sean is a typically Irish first name
CE = Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman goes along to church for some sort of religious gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiritual' reads as religious, which suits church; the event is actually a sitting to contact the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which people try to contact spirits.

clue.text: Reported volume on speaking equipment is very shaky!

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: size = volume; SEIS is said the same way
a mic (microphone) is equipment for speaking into

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the sound level on the PA system is wobbling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. 'Volume' next to a microphone suggests loudness, but here it means bulk or capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic means of earthquakes, so shaking violently.

clue.text: Play ground accommodates quiet exercise

indicators.note: ground as in crushed, so the letters of PLAY are broken up
the rearranged word makes room for another letter inside it

blocks.note: PLAY rearranged
p = piano, quiet in music; it goes in after the A

explanation.surface: A playground has room for some quiet exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play ground' reads as the single word playground; split, it is fodder plus anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of putting something to use: you exercise or apply your judgement, your rights, pressure.

clue.text: Kind to embrace darling getting reprimand

indicators.note: one word holds another in its arms

blocks.note: caring = kind
pet = darling, a favourite; it goes inside CAR…ING

explanation.surface: A gentle person hugs their sweetheart even while being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'carpeted' is British for being called in and scolded, from being summoned onto the boss's carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: an employee called onto the boss's carpet is there to be scolded, so the noun means a reprimand.

clue.text: One charging conservative customer on account

blocks.note: ac is the usual abbreviation for account; 'on' puts what follows after it
C = Conservative
a user of a service is a customer

explanation.surface: A shop charges a Tory shopper's purchases to their account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' looks like billing, which fits customer and account; it means bringing a charge against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who charges someone with wrongdoing.

clue.text: She has part in current version of Hair

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
a tress is a lock of hair, another word for it

explanation.surface: A woman has a role in a new production of the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hair look like the musical, which fits a part and a version; it is just hair.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who has a part in a play.

clue.text: Break off to deliver source of veal

blocks.note: the glaciology sense: a chunk of ice breaking away from a glacier or ice shelf
veal comes from a calf, and 'deliver' is giving birth, as a cow does

explanation.surface: Someone stops work in order to hand over a supply of veal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' sounds like a courier's job; here it is giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Calve means both to give birth to a calf and, of ice, to split away.

clue.text: Attacks credit as a silly activity

blocks.note: slaps = attacks with the hand
'on tick' is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses hitting out at credit as foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' means buying on credit, an old British phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous knockabout comedy, silly carry-on.

clue.text: Alternative theatre, first time out, to produce warmed up fare

indicators.note: another arrangement of the letters
the first T (time) is removed

blocks.note: the fodder word
t = time; the first T goes

explanation.surface: A fringe theatre company, opening for the first time, serves up reheated food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative theatre' reads as fringe drama; 'Alternative' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat is to warm up food again.

clue.text: Prohibit short-term teasing

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: ban = prohibit
TERM with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A call to outlaw brief episodes of mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-term' looks like one adjective, meaning temporary; split, it is an instruction to shorten TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: good-humoured ribbing between friends goes by either name.

clue.text: Ship in colony worker – it’s vital

blocks.note: to import is to ship goods in
a worker ant lives in a colony

explanation.surface: A worker is urgently sent by ship out to a colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colony' suggests empire, which fits shipping; it is an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Important and vital both mean essential.

clue.text: It secures request for silence on field

blocks.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow; 'on' puts SH after it
sh! asks for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone manages to get quiet on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secures' reads as obtains, fitting the request; it means holds fast, as a lead holds a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is a lead that keeps an animal secure.

clue.text: Vote in favour, blocking honour perhaps

indicators.note: the vote sits in the middle, blocking the honour

blocks.note: MBE = Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
ay (aye) is a yes vote; it goes inside M…BE

explanation.surface: A yes vote stands in the way of someone's honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour awarded in the King's lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps both express possibility.

clue.text: Seated her awkwardly where there’s a lot of water

definitions.text: where there’s a lot of water

indicators.note: the letters are placed in an awkward, different order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone sat a woman clumsily in a damp spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: any sea would fit, which is why the anagram carries the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is a large body of water between Africa and Arabia.

clue.text: Copper is more reticent and less demanding

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
shier = more shy

explanation.surface: A police officer is quieter and easier-going than colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is an easy one, so cushier means less demanding.

clue.text: Evidence of accident near waste disposal area

definitions.text: Evidence of accident near waste disposal area

blocks.note: the surface reading: traces left on the road by a vehicle that braked and slid
the setter's joke: not beside a rubbish tip but close to the body's own exit, i.e. stains in underwear

explanation.surface: Investigators find traces of a crash beside the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The waste disposal area is not a dump but the bottom; skidmarks is also British slang for stains in underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid marks are the tyre streaks left when a vehicle skids.

clue.text: King breaking cracked ice is taking a day off work!

indicators.note: the K breaks into the other letters
the ice is cracked, so its letters are broken up

blocks.note: ICE IS rearranged
K = king in chess; it goes in after SIC

explanation.surface: A monarch fell through the ice and is now off work.
explanation.walkthrough: A sickie is British and Australian slang for a day off work claimed as sick leave, often falsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a sickie is taking a day off, supposedly ill.

clue.text: Being so numerous won’t matter so much

definitions.note: the second definition splits the answer as the phrase COUNT LESS

blocks.note: too many to count
to count = to matter

explanation.surface: A large number of something makes each one less important.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single idea; the break comes between 'numerous' and 'won't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to be counted.

clue.text: Grumbled when husband leaving only hurt slightly

indicators.note: a husband who is leaving walks out, so his letter H departs from WHINGED

blocks.note: whinged is British for complained
h = husband; it is removed from WHINGED

explanation.surface: Someone moaned when their husband left, though they were barely wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: To whinge is British English for to complain peevishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wing someone is to shoot and wound them slightly, as a bird in the wing.

clue.text: Composer badly used by son

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
s = son, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A composer was mistreated by his own son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used by' reads naturally as part of the sentence, which hides it as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Frenchman who wrote Clair de lune is one instance of the class.

clue.text: Hoity-toity food with drink outside

indicators.note: the drink goes round the outside of the food

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
tuck is British schoolchild slang for food; it goes inside S…UP

explanation.surface: A snobbish meal served with drinks on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up and hoity-toity both mean snobbishly superior.

clue.text: Notice spotted showing what children can play with

blocks.note: to see = to notice
saw = spotted, the past tense

explanation.surface: A sign has been seen listing what the playground offers children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a noun, a sign; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank children ride up and down on.

clue.text: Joke about woman, strictly religious

indicators.note: the joke goes round, about, the woman

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words
any woman's name can serve; RITA goes inside PU…N

explanation.surface: A gag about a woman who is very devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' stands for a woman's first name; the crossings pin down which one.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritan describes someone strict in religion and morals.

clue.text: Busier sketches becoming central for funny show

indicators.note: take the central letters of each word

blocks.note: the middle two of BU-SI-ER
the middle two of SKE-TC-HES
the middle two of BEC-OM-ING

explanation.surface: Crowded sketches become the heart of a comedy programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' reads as a link word, but it is the third word to take letters from.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre name is short for situation comedy, so the definition describes the whole class of programme.

clue.text: Setter can be silenced but will remain unchanged

definitions.note: an adjective defined by what the thing does: something immutable will remain unchanged

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself: I'm = I am
able to be muted

explanation.surface: The setter may be shut up but won't change their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: MUTABLE is normally 'changeable'; here it is read literally as 'mute-able', which makes the surface's contrast a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by behaviour: the Latin roots mean 'not changeable', so whatever has this quality will stay as it is.

clue.text: People find bone in empty temple

indicators.note: the bone goes in the other letters
the temple is emptied of its middle, leaving T…E

blocks.note: TEMPLE without its inside letters
a rib is a bone; it goes inside T…E

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up a bone in a deserted temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' reads as deserted; it tells you to remove the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a people, a community of related families.

clue.text: Root of initial trouble up by East Riding

indicators.note: turned up, i.e. upside down, so read backwards

blocks.note: a but is an objection or snag, the first trouble raised
ER = East Riding, a former division of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The origin of a problem that started up in the East Riding.
explanation.walkthrough: The East Riding was one of the three old divisions of the English county of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen underground root or stem.

clue.text: Life with me is its own little world

blocks.note: bio = life, as in biography
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares that life with them is a world apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a partner's complaint; the definition is an ecological term.
explanation.definitionFit: A biome is a distinct natural community, such as tundra or rainforest.

clue.text: Dog soldier joins military unit without further thought

indicators.note: the unit loses the further thought

blocks.note: a corps is a military unit
a PS (postscript) is a further thought, removed from CORPS
GI = an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier impulsively signs up with an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without further thought' reads as rashly; it instructs you to drop PS.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Separated when tripping

blocks.note: set at intervals, with gaps between
dazed, as on drugs

explanation.surface: People got split up when they stumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' looks like stumbling; it is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out means both spread apart and dazed from drugs.

clue.text: My container for flower shows great skill

indicators.note: MY is the container that the flower goes in

blocks.note: taken as written
the aster is a daisy-like flower; it goes inside M…Y

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their flower vase displays real artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container for flower' reads as a vase; it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the skill of a master craftsman, as in a performance showing complete command.

clue.text: Consignee’s sales hold back description of unwarranted items

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them
the held letters read backwards

blocks.note: consig-NEE'S SA-les

explanation.surface: A consignee's sales are being held up.
explanation.walkthrough: Goods 'sold as seen' come with no guarantee: the buyer accepts them in their present condition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As seen' labels goods sold without warranty.
